title: Ziehl–Neelsen as a named acid-fast method
dek: Carbol fuchsin, acid-alcohol, methylene blue. Wikipedia's stain recipe. Smear grade and viability stay on tb-smear-culture.
story: Ziehl–Neelsen on Wikipedia is a staining method: hot carbol fuchsin, destain with acid-alcohol, counterstain. Acid-fast organisms keep fuchsin. That is the encyclopedia recipe card.
Fluorochrome auramine methods are the high-throughput cousin. Neither stain is a species, a viability assay, or a RIF result.
IUATLD/WHO smear grading is clinic plate territory. Wikipedia may show pretty rods; it will not replace a WRD-first algorithm.
deep: Nocardia can be partially acid-fast. Dead Mtb can still stain.
Kinyoun is a cold variant of the same idea.
Do not skip NAAT because the smear is pretty.
Biosafety of making smears is infection-control, not this recipe.
